# No CI check compiles the App worker from an installed copy

## Context

PR #18851 (#18849) fixes three portal views whose `marked` import resolved only at the repository root. In a consumer, `build-all` failed on them with three `Module not found`. No check in this repository could have failed on it. The same class — a specifier that resolves at the repository root but not in an installed copy — produced `#17868`, `#17943` and `#17997`.

## The Problem

The one check that builds this package from outside itself, `check-consumer-runtime-build`, never compiles the App worker:

- `buildWorker()` in `buildScripts/util/check-consumer-runtime-build.mjs` compiles `configFactory({worker: 'data', insideNeo: 'false'})`, plus Main.
- Its `marked` coverage is a list. `createFixture()` writes `apps/probe/data/ConsumerOnly.mjs`, which imports the two `src/` importers by name (`component/Markdown`, `app/content/Component`). The three portal importers were not on the list.
- `.github/workflows/consumer-runtime-build.yml` is path-filtered, and no path under `apps/`, `examples/` or `docs/app/` is in the filter. A PR that edits only portal files does not run it.

The engine's own `build-all` job (#18835) cannot see the class: at the repository root, the old specifier resolves.

## The Architectural Reality

- The App worker's `importApp()` (`src/worker/App.mjs`) is one lazy context over `(apps|docs/app|examples|src)/**/app.mjs`, and its `webpackExclude` keeps `node_modules/neo.mjs`. *Corrected while implementing:* in consumer mode the App config (`webpack.config.appworker.mjs`) moves that context to the workspace root. There, webpack's context walk rewrites every `./node_modules/…` file to a bare request that the context's `^\.\/` regExp drops, so the context reaches no shipped app. The Institution compiled the portal views (#18849's `./node_modules/neo.mjs/apps/portal/...`) because its `build-all` runs `all.mjs -f -n`, which is framework mode. create-app's template runs `all.mjs -n`. Compiling the App config as the framework from an installed copy reaches every shipped app, with no list to maintain.
- The workflow header records why the check packs, installs and compiles for real: a path-reasoning probe passed where a physical build failed. This ticket extends the physical build and keeps that decision.
- The check installs from `npm pack`, so `.npmignore` applies. `apps/**/*.mjs` is excluded except for listed apps, and `apps/portal` is listed (`!/apps/portal/**/*.mjs`). A tarball's App-worker compile therefore reaches the same portal views the Institution's git install compiled.
- Current job: 72–81 s on GitHub runners (last 5 runs, 2026-09-16/17).

## The Fix

`check-consumer-runtime-build` also compiles the App worker's own config (`webpack.config.appworker.mjs`) from the installed copy, as the framework standing in the consumer, in at least one mode, and fails on any compile error. `consumer-runtime-build.yml` runs on PRs that touch the App worker's context roots. Widen the path filter, or drop it if the job fits the budget.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The check compiles the App worker from the installed package and fails on any webpack error.
- [ ] Red first: with one of PR #18851's three specifiers reverted, the check fails and names that file. Restored, it passes.
- [ ] A PR that changes only `apps/portal/**` runs the job.
- [ ] Job wall-clock stays ≤ 5 min on GitHub runners, measured over ≥ 3 runs (operator budget, 2026-09-18).
- [ ] The fixture's two hand-listed `marked` importers are deleted if the App-worker compile covers them, or the PR says why they stay.

## Out of Scope

- Whether a consumer's App worker should reach the engine's own `apps/` at all (#18849's out-of-scope: whether `apps/portal` ships).
- A static lint for relative `node_modules/` specifiers.

## Avoided Traps

- **A specifier grep as the guard.** It catches one spelling of the class. It cannot report a target the installed package does not contain (an npmignored path), which a build from the installed copy reports as `Module not found`.
